text:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran the holdout suite for the new 'sherlock' embedding (v0.3) quantized to int8 on quasar-bench. recall@5 is down ~4.6% vs v0.2 on short queries. Not huge but consistent across seeds. anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw the same in staging yesterday, flagged in the eval dashboard. recall@1 drop is smaller (~2%), so precision-ish shift.

lee: do we have cluster-level metrics? could be centroid drift -> affects recall@k.

alex: posted the quick diff: https://internal/reports/embeds/sherlock/v0.3/int8/diff — looks like avg norm of vectors dropped 0.07 which could change cosine thresholds.

maria: hmm that matches. I also noticed silhouette score down 0.03 for k=50 on wiki-small holdout.

sam: can we repro deterministically? run id: run-2026-03-20-0845 on ci. ci-bot: evaluation finished — artifacts at s3://redwood-eval/sherlock/v0.3/int8/run-2026-03-20-0845/

lee: quick checks: 1) compare L2 norms distribution, 2) check whitening/normalization step (we recently toggled postnorm in the pipeline), 3) rerun with fp16 model but same quant config to separate quant vs model change.

alex: command I ran to reproduce locally:
```bash
python eval/recall.py --model sherlock:v0.3 --quant int8 --dataset quasar-bench --k 5 --seed 42 --normalize True
```
outputs attached in the report.

maria: i can take the whitening angle. quick question: did we change the embedding head scaling between v0.2 and v0.3?

alex: small change — we removed a layernorm before pool in v0.3 (PR #842) to improve latency. Might explain norm shift.

sam: that PR was primarily for speed, yes. Could be that + quantization interaction. Can we try v0.3 + force-postnorm hook to see if recall recovers?

lee: i'm running a tweak now (force post-norm after pooling) — starting job on staging-gpu-4. will post results.

ci-bot: job start: eval-job-6573 (staging-gpu-4). logs: https://ci/redwood/jobs/6573/logs

alex: if post-norm recovers recall, we might keep v0.3 but reintroduce normalization as a cheap patch — preferable to reverting PR for latency. But need to check cluster geometry (does it affect nearest-neighbor ordering?).

maria: agreed. also let's run a small clustering stability test: sample 5k queries, compute UMAP + kmeans, compare cluster assignments Jaccard vs v0.2. I can spin that up.

sam: FYI I ran a quick ablation: v0.3 fp16 (no quant) had only 0.8% recall@5 drop vs v0.2 fp16. So quant amplifies the effect.

lee: interesting — suggests quantization sensitivity. Could be per-channel vs per-tensor quant settings. Alex, what quant backend did you use for the int8 build?

alex: using onnxruntime-static int8 symmetric per-channel (our new fast path).

maria: okay plan: (1) lee will test post-norm patch (staging job), (2) sam will run v0.3 with per-tensor quant config to compare, (3) i will run clustering stability / UMAP Jaccard test on 5k sample. reconvene in ~2 hrs.

sam: noted. tagging @eng-ml for visibility :eyes:

lee: staging job done — recall@5 recovered ~3.9% of the delta (now only -0.7% vs v0.2). silhouette improved a bit. logs: https://ci/redwood/jobs/6573/artifacts/metrics.json

maria: thanks — that's promising. alex can you try per-tensor quant next?

alex: running per-tensor now (job 6574). will post when done.

ci-bot: job finished: eval-job-6574. summary: v0.3 + per-tensor int8 -> recall@5 -1.2% vs v0.2. artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/sherlock/v0.3/int8-per-tensor/6574/

sam: okay that points at quant per-channel interactions being worse. we should update the quant recommendation for sherlock v0.3 in the model catalog until we have a better fast path.

maria: agreed — i'll open a catalog note and a rollback guard in the rollout policy that pins int8 to per-tensor for now.

alex: opened GH issue #981 with experiments and suggested fixes (postnorm hook + per-tensor fallback).

lee: nice. if anyone wants to reproduce locally: dataset sample and seed in s3 path above.

maria: thanks team. follow-ups: leave run artifacts and small writeup in the model onboarding doc (docs/models/sherlock/onboard.md). i'll update later today. :thumbsup:
